unfinished_ok.exception: the console's kernel numbers its user code selectors its own way: 32-bit code is 0x33 and 64-bit 0x43 (docs/IA32_DESIGN.md), where Windows has 0x23 and 0x33. test_context_exception_request, the file's last test, enters 64-bit code with "push $0x33; lret" (call_func64), which on the console stays in 32-bit mode and runs the 64-bit bytes as 32-bit code; their access violation reaches the test's own vectored handler, which waits for a step the main thread never takes (trace b13-exc32-053728: AV at code_mem with cs 0x33, handler entered, no return until the 300 s timeout). A selector the kernel accepts raises nothing to catch: a platform limit for any 32-bit program that enters 64-bit code by a hard-coded selector
